propositions: Compaction writes SNAPSHOT.json and *.retired files to the working tree without atomicity or rollback, leaving the tracker dirty when interrupted.
The next reconverge union-merge fails with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' when origin has already committed those regenerable paths, causing a permanent wedge.
Push recovery cannot clear untracked files (git reset --hard is tracked-only; git stash without -u does not rescue untracked paths), so every retry re-aborts identically.

The union-merge handler must detect the untracked-overwrite abort signature, relocate only the named untracked paths to a quarantine directory outside the worktree, and retry the merge once to keep both parents and preserve local commits.
Genuine content conflicts and other merge failures must fall back to today's abort-only behavior with the fsck-recover hint, ensuring no regression in conflict handling.
